blocks.text: Why a Chauffeur Makes Sense in San Bernardino
Three practical reasons, specific to this city.
blocks.html: Three practical reasons, specific to this city.

items: San Bernardino is a sprawling, low-density city where nothing is walkable and event venues sit 5-10 miles apart.
The National Orange Show grounds can hold 40,000 attendees and park roughly 8,000 cars, so a vehicle-per-group model reaches far more people per driver.
Downtown's historic core and the fairgrounds are separate destinations about 10 minutes apart by car, not on foot.
The I-10, I-215 and SR 210 interchanges back up badly during evening events.
San Bernardino International Airport offers local commercial service, and Ontario Intl is about 12 miles west.

blocks.text: We also quote San Bernardino to the hour rather than the trip. Most groups need four hours, and four is the standard minimum across the industry because a committed vehicle cannot be sold to anyone else while it is parked at your venue. If your night genuinely needs less, ask for a one-way transfer rate instead of paying a full minimum.

blocks.text: Choosing a Vehicle for a San Bernardino Night

Capacity is the first filter, then cost per person. A stretch limo seats 6 to 8, a Chrysler 300 about 8, a Hummer 12, and a Sprinter limo up to 14. Our party bus seats 24. Below about ten people, two cars or a limo usually beats a bus. Above ten, the bus wins on cost per head and nobody gets left behind.

blocks.text: Licensed, Insured, and Backup Plans

Every chauffeur on our team is licensed and background checked, and our vehicles are licensed and inspected. Our drivers work the night and do not drink, which matters when the group includes teenagers, and we set a fixed return time off the venue's posted close so nobody is standing in a parking lot at 1 AM wondering where the car went.
